name: node-sql-parser
license_evidence: package.json license Apache-2.0 and LICENSE (Apache License 2.0) in the pinned npm tarball
input_api: new Parser().astify(local UTF-8 text, {database: 'postgresql'}) from node-sql-parser/build/postgresql
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. The package's other database grammars are untested.
family: node-sql-parser PEG.js grammars (one generated parser per database)
family_note: build/postgresql.js bundles the parser that PEG.js generates from pegjs/postgresql.pegjs plus the package's src helpers. astify returns plain AST objects (type select/insert, columns, from with join entries, where, groupby, orderby, values). The adapter reads those fields and walks the AST for aggr_func/function names and number/single_quote_string literals. Independent of pgsql-ast-parser (nearley) and the libpg_query WASM packages. @florajs/sql-parser is an older fork.

popularity.limitation: Package downloads include all bundled database grammars and transitive installs.

name: pgsql-ast-parser
license_evidence: package.json license MIT in the pinned npm tarball (no LICENSE file is shipped)
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary.
family: pgsql-ast-parser nearley grammar and moo lexer
family_note: parse runs the package's compiled nearley grammar and moo-based lexer (bundled in index.js, with the nearley runtime and moo as dependencies) and returns typed AST objects (select columns/from/join/where/groupBy/orderBy, insert into/columns/values). The adapter reads those fields and walks call, integer/numeric and string nodes. Independent of node-sql-parser (PEG.js) and libpg_query.

popularity.limitation: Package downloads include transitive installs (for example through pg-mem).

name: sql-parser-cst
license_evidence: package.json license GPL-2.0-or-later and the GNU GPL version 2 LICENSE text in the pinned npm tarball
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 and parsed with the sqlite dialect; the trailing empty statement after ';' is not counted. Valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary.
family_note: parse runs the package's own Peggy-generated parser (lib/parser.js, about 179,000 lines) and returns a concrete syntax tree that keeps keywords, aliases and parentheses (select_stmt clauses, join_expr, alias, func_call, number_literal, string_literal; insert_clause and values_clause). The adapter reads those clauses and walks func_call and literal nodes. It has no runtime dependencies and is independent of node-sql-parser (PEG.js), pgsql-ast-parser (nearley) and libpg_query. MySQL, MariaDB, BigQuery and PostgreSQL are documented as experimental and untested here.

popularity.limitation: Package downloads include transitive installs (for example through prettier-plugin-sql-cst).

name: dt-sql-parser
license_evidence: package.json license MIT and the MIT LICENSE file in the pinned npm tarball
input_api: new MySQL().parse(local UTF-8 text, errorListener) -> ProgramContext
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 and parsed by the MySQL class with an error listener; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. A resolve hook completes the package's extensionless ES module imports without changing package files.
family_note: MySQL.parse runs the package's ANTLR4-generated MySqlLexer and MySqlParser (dist/lib/mysql, about 90,000 lines, on the antlr4ng runtime) and returns the concrete ANTLR parse tree. The adapter reads rule contexts by the grammar's rule names (querySpecification, selectElement, tableName, joinPart, groupByItem, orderByExpression, aggregateWindowedFunction, decimalLiteral, stringLiteral, insertStatement, expressionsWithDefaults). The published dist uses extensionless ES module imports meant for bundlers, so the harness registers a resolve hook that retries those relative specifiers with '.js' or '/index.js'. Independent of node-sql-parser, pgsql-ast-parser, sql-parser-cst and libpg_query; the other dialect classes (Flink, Spark, Hive, PostgreSQL, Trino, Impala, generic) are untested.

popularity.limitation: Package downloads include transitive installs (for example through monaco-sql-languages).

name: sqlite-parser
license_evidence: package.json license MIT and the MIT LICENSE file in the pinned npm tarball
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 and passed to the synchronous sqliteParser call; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary.
family_note: sqliteParser runs the package's PEG.js-generated SQLite grammar (lib/parser.js, shipped minified without a source map) with its own tracer and returns an AST (statement variant select/insert, result, from map with join entries, where, group, order, function and literal nodes). The adapter reads those fields. Released 2017 (last release). @appland/sql-parser is a separately maintained fork with a modified grammar (same AST shape). Independent of node-sql-parser, pgsql-ast-parser, sql-parser-cst, dt-sql-parser and libpg_query.

name: @appland/sql-parser
license_evidence: package.json license MIT and the MIT LICENSE file in the pinned npm tarball
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 and passed to the synchronous sqliteParser call; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary.
family_note: AppLand's fork of sqlite-parser (repository applandinc/sqlite-parser, release 1.5.1 from 2022) ships its own PEG.js-generated parser, minified without a source map, and keeps sqlite-parser's API and AST shape; the adapter is the sqlite-parser adapter with the package name changed. Overlap with the selected sqlite-parser 1.0.1: the generated parser is 127,259 bytes against 109,981, about 51% of sqlite-parser's statement fragments occur unchanged in it (43% of the fork's), and the index, tracer and streaming wrappers differ only in the version banner. It is a separately maintained fork with grammar changes, not a byte-identical copy or a rename. Independent of node-sql-parser, pgsql-ast-parser, sql-parser-cst, dt-sql-parser and libpg_query.

popularity.limitation: Captured in the round-2 extension (round_2_metric) with the same window as round 1; downloads include transitive installs (for example through AppMap tooling).

name: sqllens
license_evidence: package.json license MIT and the MIT LICENSE file in the pinned npm tarball; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md records the forked grammars' own licenses (PostgreSQL grammar: BSD-3-Clause, antlr/grammars-v4)
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes decoded as strict UTF-8 and parsed with the postgres dialect; any syntax error rejects the input; the summary is read from the returned CST. Valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary.
family: sqllens ANTLR4 grammars (PostgreSQL grammar forked from antlr/grammars-v4)
family_note: parse runs the package's ANTLR4-generated PostgresLexer and PostgresParser (dist/generated/postgres, on the antlr4ng runtime) and returns the token stream, a syntax-error count, the concrete parse tree (cst, documented as the escape hatch) and a lowered dialect-neutral IR. The IR marks INSERT as unsupported ('non-query'), so the adapter reads both controls from the CST by rule-context class (Simple_select_pramary, Target_list, Relation_expr, Joined_table, Where_clause, Group_by_item, Sortby, Func_name, Iconst, Fconst, Anysconst, Insertstmt, Insert_column_item, Values_clause, Expr_list). Its grammars are forks of upstream ANTLR grammars (PostgreSQL from antlr/grammars-v4); dt-sql-parser is a separate ANTLR4 package with its own grammar sources, and its selected path uses MySQL. Independent of node-sql-parser, pgsql-ast-parser, sql-parser-cst, sqlite-parser and libpg_query.

popularity.limitation: Captured in the round-2 extension (round_2_metric) with the same window as round 1; downloads include transitive installs.
